Local fork of github.com/markusmobius/go-dateparser v1.4.7.

Upstream source and BSD-3-Clause LICENSE are preserved. This application uses
Go 1.26; remove the optional upstream toolchain go1.27.1 preference. No compiler
installation is required by this fork.

The generated internal/data locale initialization bodies are unchanged. Their
205 init functions are renamed initializeLocale_<file>; zz-lazy.go calls them in
the same lexical source-file order once, on the first GetLocaleData call.
All locales are retained. The once barrier protects concurrent first readers.
The concurrent first-lookup test covers 256 callers and eight locales.

This avoids allocating all language tables in every short-lived Go plugin
process. The host still loads those tables on its first date lookup; this is
not a claim that parsing itself uses no memory or that production peak RSS
has been measured. Generated tables and parsing behavior are not replaced.

The upstream generator is retained unchanged. Regeneration requires reapplying
this local patch and running the upstream library, cold-concurrency and actual
application checks; zz-lazy.go deliberately fails to build if renamed generated
constructors are lost. See docs/site-dateparser-resource-initialization.txt.
